Fill the grid so every row and column has the right number of ship squares and the whole fleet fits.
Each puzzle has exactly one solution, so you never have to guess.
Ships cannot be placed on islands or reefs, and a torpedo stops at an island but passes over a reef.
Islands and reefs may sit right next to a ship.
Sonar reads the 3×3 area around the square you choose and counts the enemy ship squares still unhit there.
It cannot see islands, reefs or mines.
Each turn has a time limit: 8 seconds on Easy, 6 on Medium and 4 on Hard.
Pausing or leaving the app freezes the clock.
A mine sinks nothing, but hitting one costs you your next turn.
Mines are never placed next to a ship, so the automatic water never lies.
A plane checks a whole row or column and tells you whether any unhit ship square is on the surface, decoys included.
The fleet includes seaplanes, with a T-shaped hull of four squares, and one-square midget submarines.
These rules can be combined with the others.
Three freighters sail with your fleet, and enough of them must stay afloat for the number of rounds shown.
Sinking the enemy first also wins, but losing too many freighters or your whole fleet ends the mission.
A decoy is a fake ship placed before the battle: when the enemy hits it, the wreck is revealed at the end of their next turn.
A decoy never counts toward your fleet or the victory.
A torpedo runs from the edge of the sea along one row or column until it hits a ship, an island or a mine.
Reefs do not stop it, and a mine it sets off costs you no turn.
Submarines start on the surface and dive for two rounds out of every four.
A shot at a submerged submarine only reveals a contact and does no damage.
Once per battle, you can repair a hit square of a ship that is still afloat, and it becomes intact again.
The enemy learns that a square was repaired, and it must be hit again.
A salvo fires one shot for each ship you still have afloat, decoys excluded, with a minimum of one.
The shots resolve one by one, in order.
A cross barrage fires at a central square and the four squares beside it: five shots at once.
Squares outside the sea or already fired are skipped, and a mine costs only one turn.
The sea has 12 by 12 squares, so the fleet has far more places to hide.
Search the whole sea instead of working from one corner.
Fog fades your water marks four of your turns after you make them, while hits, sunk ships, automatic water, contacts and readings stay.
A faded square still counts as a shot if you fire at it again.
Once per battle, each side may move one of its ships to a new place.
The enemy learns that a ship moved but not where, and old marks stay because they were true when made.
